questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body moving along a circular path with constant speed has:
questions.explanation: Speed is constant but the direction of velocity keeps changing, so there is a centripetal acceleration v²/r pointing towards the centre.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 3: Motion in a Plane

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A cricketer moves his hands backwards while catching a fast ball. This reduces the force on his hands because it:
options: Increases the mass of the ball
Reduces the ball's kinetic energy to zero instantly
questions.explanation: The change in momentum is fixed by the ball's speed, so F = Δp/Δt is lowered only by stretching the time of impact.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 4: Laws of Motion

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. The image formed is:
options: Real, inverted and of the same size
questions.explanation: The object sits exactly at the centre of curvature (2f = 30 cm), so the image also forms at 2f, real, inverted and of the same size.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 9: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which concentration term is independent of temperature?
questions.explanation: Molality uses the mass of solvent, and mass does not change with temperature, whereas molarity depends on volume, which expands on heating.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 1: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to molecular orbital theory, the O₂ molecule is paramagnetic because it has:
options: Two unpaired electrons in antibonding pi orbitals
questions.explanation: The last two electrons of O₂ go singly into the degenerate π*2p orbitals with parallel spins, which valence bond theory could not explain.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 4: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Tollens' reagent gives a silver mirror with:
questions.explanation: Tollens' reagent oxidises aldehydes and deposits metallic silver. Ketones such as acetone and benzophenone give no reaction.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 12, Chapter 8: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Removal of the shoot apex leads to the growth of lateral buds. This shows that the apex is the source of:
questions.explanation: Auxin made at the apex suppresses lateral buds, which is why tea bushes and hedges are pruned to make them bushy.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 13: Plant Growth and Development

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The Hershey and Chase experiment with bacteriophages conclusively proved that:
options: Both DNA and protein carry genes
questions.explanation: Phages labelled with radioactive phosphorus passed their DNA into the bacteria, while sulphur labelled protein coats stayed outside, so DNA carries heredity.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The part of the retina that has only cones and gives the sharpest vision is the:
questions.explanation: The fovea centralis is a thinned pit packed with cones, so an image focused there is seen in greatest detail; the optic disc has no photoreceptors at all.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 18: Neural Control and Coordination

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Benign tumours differ from malignant tumours in that benign tumours:
options: Remain confined to their original site and do not metastasise
Spread to distant organs through blood
Always grow faster than malignant tumours
questions.explanation: Malignant cells invade surrounding tissue and travel in the blood to start secondary tumours, a process called metastasis, which is what makes cancer life threatening.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 7: Human Health and Disease
